title: Reasoning or Rambling? Exploring the Effect of Thinking on Agent Persuasion
abstract: arXiv:2509.21054v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Understanding persuasion is critical for the safety and reliability of multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs). This paper studies persuasion dynamics by contrasting general LLMs with Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) that employ explicit ``thinking'' processes. Through large-scale experiments on objective (MMLU) and subjective (PersuasionBench and Perspectrum) tasks, we identify Persuasion Duality: reasoning enhances an agent's persuasive power while simultaneously increasing its resistance to persuasion. For LRMs, adding thinking content increases persuasion rates by 21 pp on average, yet reduces susceptibility to incorrect persuasion by up to 10 pp on objective tasks. Despite these gains, we uncover a critical vulnerability: persuasiveness often stems from superficial cues such as response length and repetition rather than logical validity. translated_title: 推理还是胡言乱语？探究思考对智能体说服力的影响
translated_abstract: arXiv:2509.21054v2 公告类型：交叉替换  摘要：理解说服力对于基于大型语言模型（LLMs）的多智能体系统的安全性和可靠性至关重要。本文通过对比通用LLMs与采用显式“思考”过程的大型推理模型（LRMs）来研究说服动态。通过在客观任务（MMLU）和主观任务（PersuasionBench和Perspectrum）上进行大规模实验，我们发现了说服双重性：推理增强了智能体的说服力，同时提高了其抵抗说服的能力。对于LRMs，添加思考内容使说服率平均提高了21个百分点，但在客观任务上，对错误说服的敏感性降低了最多10个百分点。尽管有这些收益，我们揭示了一个关键脆弱性：说服力往往源于表面线索，如回答长度和重复，而非逻辑有效性。非语义填充或重复结论可以匹配甚至超越说服效果。
tldr: 本文发现推理模型在增强说服力的同时提高抗说服性，但说服力常依赖表面线索而非逻辑有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that reasoning models enhance persuasion while increasing resistance, yet persuasiveness often relies on superficial cues rather than logical validity.
